tested_on.host: Hermes agent on an openclawlaunch Linux container: 16 vCPU, 62 GiB RAM, 38 GB free disk at slice end (headless-Linux numbers only; real-device behavior is NOT_RUN)

new_dependencies: none — S2 adds zero npm dependencies (package-lock.json unchanged; package.json only gains the build_pwa_precache step). The PWA surface is hand-built: manifest.webmanifest, a ~130-line classic service worker (public/sw.js), a build-time precache-manifest generator (scripts/build_pwa_precache.mjs) and deterministic icons (scripts/generate_icons.mjs).

pwa_decision.chosen: purpose-built classic-script service worker + static manifest, no PWA library
rejected: vite-plugin-pwa / Workbox generateSW — its precache glob runs at vite-build time, but this app's OCR runtime is fetched into dist/ocr-assets/ AFTER the vite build (scripts/fetch_ocr_assets.mjs, pinned + hash-verified), so a workbox precache would miss exactly the files offline OCR needs unless the build order were restructured around the library

a bundled/ES-module service worker — module SW support differs across engines and importScripts() of the generated precache list keeps the worker a plain classic script every engine with SW support can run unchanged
pwa_decision.share_target_privacy: the worker parses the multipart POST in memory, reads ONLY the file field named in the manifest's share_target params, hands the image to a window client via postMessage, and never caches, stores or logs the request or its body (asserted by the a08 cache-exactness check: the app-shell cache contains exactly the build's precache entries afterwards)

app_shell.cache_name: precache-v1 (matches the A15 allow-list patterns in src/privacy/audit.ts)
app_shell.generator: scripts/build_pwa_precache.mjs — sha256 revision per file, cache key url + ?__pcv=<rev12> so fixed-name files bust on every deploy; the SW itself and the manifest are never precached
app_shell.offline_measured: after first load, context.setOffline(true) + reload renders the shell with zero failed requests, and a pick runs real OCR offline in BOTH engines (a11_offline_ocr_after_first_load)

icons.generated_by: scripts/generate_icons.mjs — headless Chromium renders the deterministic CSS mark (192/512 + a maskable safe-zone variant); committed output, CI never regenerates; pixel-verified programmatically (dimensions, dark shell #101418, light-blue glyph center, 900+ distinct colors)

clipboard_capabilities_measured.chromium: with context permissions clipboard-read/clipboard-write granted: clipboard.write(image) works, clipboard.read() returns image/png, dispatched ClipboardEvent('paste') carries the file; with the grants revoked (permissions: []): read() is refused with NotAllowedError — the A10 denial flow is real
clipboard_capabilities_measured.webkit: clipboard.write(image) is accepted without any permission; clipboard.read() is platform-denied (NotAllowedError — Playwright's WebKit grants no clipboard permissions); dispatched ClipboardEvent('paste') carries the file AND the app processes it (review screen appears); real Ctrl/Cmd+V round-trip of writeText text works

ocr_engine: unchanged from S0/S1 (tesseract.js 7.0.0, cacheMethod 'none'); S2's service-worker precache now covers /ocr-assets/, so the 2 MB pinned traineddata that S1 re-fetched per fresh session is served from the app-shell cache after the first load — including offline.
